extracted.intended_audience: legal researchers, journalists, consumers, and members of the public seeking information about FTC enforcement cases
extracted.subtask_description: An agency web page that lists Federal Trade Commission cases and proceedings, providing metadata (status, docket numbers), short summaries of allegations and remedies, and links to related documents. Designed to help users find and refine information about FTC enforcement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion criterion for Cases and Proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Every year the FTC brings hundreds of cases against individuals and companies for violating consumer protection and competition laws that the agency enforces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This page collects cases the FTC has brought in federal court or through its internal administrative process (adjudicative proceedings). Categories include matters involving fraud, scams, identity theft, false advertising, privacy violations, anti-competitive behavior and more.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case title / parties identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Each entry shows the case caption or title (e.g., 'Valvoline Inc./Greenbriar Equity Fund V, L.P', 'Uber, FTC v.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles identify the parties involved and the matter name so users can quickly recognize the subject of the listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of Action
rubrics_metrics.description: Field labeled 'Type of Action' indicating the forum or procedural posture (examples on page: Administrative, Federal, Adjudicative Proceedings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes how the matter is being pursued (e.g., internal administrative action vs. federal court lawsuit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Last Updated
rubrics_metrics.description: Field labeled 'Last Updated' showing the date the record or summary was most recently updated (e.g., May 7, 2026).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides currency of the information and helps users sort or filter by recency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket Number
rubrics_metrics.description: Field labeled 'Docket Number' listing the docket or proceeding number assigned to the matter (e.g., 9451, C-4824, 3:25-cv-03477).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables precise identification and cross-referencing with court or Commission records.

rubrics_metrics.name: FTC Matter/File Number
rubrics_metrics.description: Field labeled 'FTC Matter/File Number' when applicable (examples: 251 0058, 2423092).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency-specific identifier for internal tracking and public reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case Status
rubrics_metrics.description: Field labeled 'Case Status' indicating current posture (example shown: Pending).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conveys whether matters are pending, settled, closed, etc., to inform users about current state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summaries must state allegations and legal bases
rubrics_metrics.description: Case summaries should describe the core allegations and the legal provisions claimed to be violated (example: 'The complaint alleges that Uber charges consumers ... in violation of the FTC Act and ROSCA' and cites 'Section 5 of the FTC Act' and the 'Restore Online Shoppers’ Confidence Act').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summaries should name statutes/rules alleged to be violated and the factual basis of the claim so readers understand the nature of the enforcement action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summaries should include remedies or settlement terms
rubrics_metrics.description: When available, the entry summarizes remedies or settlement terms (examples: divestiture of 45 quick-lube shops; settlement requires ESI to adopt fundamental business-practice changes; prohibition on selling sensitive location data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the relief obtained or required (injunctions, divestitures, monetary relief, business practice changes) so users see the enforcement outcome or proposed remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summaries should identify alleged consumer harm or conduct type
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries highlight the alleged harmful conduct or consumer impact (examples: charging without consent, making cancellation difficult, artificially inflating insulin list prices, selling sensitive location data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate the nature of consumer harm to contextualize the enforcement priority (e.g., deception, privacy violations, anticompetitive rebating).

rubrics_metrics.name: Document attachments and commissioner statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Some entries link to attached files such as 'Statement of Commissioner Mark R. Meador In the Matter of...' with date and author information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide downloadable documents, statements, or filings and identify their authors and file sizes for transparency and further reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display, filtering, and sorting controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Interface options shown: 'Refine your results', 'Show: 20 50 100', 'Sort By: Newest Relevance', and pagination controls (page numbers, Next page, Last page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows users to control result set size, sort order, and navigate through large numbers of entries (the page displays 'Displaying 1 - 20 of 6077').

rubrics_metrics.name: Pagination and result counts
rubrics_metrics.description: The page displays the range and total count of results (e.g., 'Displaying 1 - 20 of 6077') and provides pagination links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicates scope of the archive and supports navigation through many records; useful for users and citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of concise lead sentences in case summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Case entries open with short descriptive lead sentences summarizing the core case (e.g., 'The Federal Trade Commission will require automotive services company Valvoline Inc. ... to divest 45 quick-lube oil change shops to resolve antitrust concerns surrounding their $625 million deal.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Front-load the most important facts (who, what, remedy) so readers can quickly grasp the case's essence.
